purpose: Restore and harden the exact-main REG.RU release chain. Keep every production self-hosted job non-root, actionless and without Docker authority; use only the restricted root controller for mutation; transfer bounded redacted preflight evidence to a hosted publisher while validating and checksumming activation, finalization and deployment evidence locally on REG.RU; fail closed before and after every production mutation.
requiredBehavior: keep the self-hosted runner non-root without Docker socket authority
execute no third-party GitHub Action on any production self-hosted preflight activation finalization or deployment job
delegate every production mutation to the root-owned restricted controller
export only bounded valid JSON redacted preflight evidence through a job output
materialize and validate preflight evidence only on the hosted status-publishing job
validate target binding and terminal state of activation finalization and deployment evidence on REG.RU
checksum activation SSE finalization and deployment evidence without printing evidence contents
fail preflight when the upstream canonical image build is not a successful main push
require successful completion of the exact upstream preflight workflow attempt and every critical job before activation without mislabelling inventory completion as readiness PASS
require successful completion of the exact upstream activation workflow attempt and every critical job before standalone deployment
bind manual activation and deployment to explicit exact upstream run IDs and attempts instead of reusable commit statuses
make every non-PR workflow fail when any production-chain job is failed or skipped
make the PC-CROP scope guard honor only exact branch mappings backed by a matching concurrent scope authority on PR and main push events
register the merged PostgreSQL authority branch and its exact three source paths
stop before every production mutation when an upstream authority check is absent or mismatched
preserve automatic rollback when activation acceptance or TAI deployment postflight fails
